The Incident of Seven Men of the Ansaar Martyred During the Battle of Uhud

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when the Mushrikeen surrounded Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Uhud, Rasulullaah ﷺ was with seven men from the Ansaar and one from the Quraysh. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Who will repulse them from us and be my companion in Jannah?" An Ansaari stepped forward and fought until he was martyred. When the Mushrikeen again surrounded Rasulullaah ﷺ, he again announced, "Who will repulse them from us and be my companion in Jannah?" (Another Ansaari went forward and fought until he was also martyred. Rasulullaah ﷺ and the others were repeatedly surrounded and repulsed by each one of the seven Ansaar until) Eventually all seven had been martyred. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "We have not been fair to our companions (by leaving them to fight single-handedly)."[^2]

Another narration from Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) states that after being overwhelmed during the Battle of Uhud, the Muslims dispersed from around Rasulullaah ﷺ and the only people with him were eleven men from the Ansaar and Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydillaah (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ had begun climbing the mountain when the Mushrikeen caught up with him. Rasulullaah ﷺ then asked, "Is there none to repulse them?" "I am here, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" responded Hadhrat Talha (RA). "Stay where you are, O Talha," Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed. One of the Ansaar then said, "I shall, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" As the Ansaari fought in their defence, Rasulullaah ﷺ and the others with him continued climbing. The Ansaari was eventually martyred and the Mushrikeen were again catching up with Rasulullaah ﷺ.

Rasulullaah ﷺ again asked, "Is there none to repulse them?" When Hadhrat Talha (RA) again volunteered for the task, Rasulullaah ﷺ gave him the same instruction as before. One of the Ansaar said, "Then I shall, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" As the Ansaari fought in their defence, the others continued climbing. This Ansaari was also martyred and the Mushrikeen again started catching up with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ then repeated his request as before (every time an Ansaari was martyred defending them) to which Hadhrat Talha (RA) repeatedly volunteered himself. Rasulullaah ﷺ however, kept holding him back, to which an Ansaari volunteered himself and received permission to fight. Each one then fought as the others had fought until none but Hadhrat Talha (RA) was left with Rasulullaah ﷺ.
